# Local Projects

A WhaleIsle Project links one existing local directory to one lasting coordinator conversation. Add Project from the new-conversation directory menu and choose a directory. Repeating the same canonical directory opens its original Project and coordinator. Non-Git directories work without initialization. Creation starts no model and creates no worker or branch. Its coordinator is the native Team Lead. The Project category also exposes the same add action.

The main surface remains the native conversation, composer and model controls. Ask questions, request work, add conditions and stop work there. The coordinator directly answers questions supported by known facts or existing results and delegates actual work to continuing workers. Workstream IDs stay internal; follow-up uses the original worker Session, cwd and history. Worker processes and files run locally; model requests use the configured provider.

## Runtime

New `project_request` calls may omit `requestId` or supply an empty string; both receive the same call-derived identity. A nonempty identity revises only that Project's existing requirement. When reading a v2 catalog written by the former empty-string bug, the Host restores an identity only when its owning Project, original authorization versions and all empty references match uniquely. It retains the former ID and originating call as recovery metadata, preserves the original requirements and execution records, and follows normal paused cold recovery. Conflicting identities keep the original catalog untouched and report that it needs review.

`project-coordinator` exposes `project_request`, `project_queue`, `project_read_store`, `project_delegate`, `project_deliver`, `project_stop` and scoped native Team reads. Its cwd is `$DSH_HOME/projects/<projectId>`, distinct from the directory displayed as the Project’s work object. Existing `session/presentation.owner = 'project'` supplies display ownership. The coordinator keeps a normal editable composer and is not attached as a member of the code Workspace. Rename and archive shortcuts route through the Project owner rather than ordinary Session operations; the Lead cannot be forked into an unowned coordinator.

Each worker uses the independent `project-worker` preset and the existing fresh, continuable `spawn` provider. A caller-reserved childId is persisted before native creation. Existing workers receive assignments through the native Team mailbox. A recorded failure or confirmed missing original Session can require an explicit replacement with a reason and exact previous assignment; it receives its own member identity and retains the original history. Normal continuation preserves the member. The native descriptor preserves the cwd, preset, model route and narrow Project admission policy on cold continuation. The native Team Lead log owns membership, tasks and mailbox. Additive `team/control` records bind the Project host policy, cold capacity, cancelled messages, immutable assignment identities and explicit failed-member retry. No parallel worker execution engine is introduced.

Each delegation records its actual coordinator user-message and tool-call identity. A model request ID is not authorization. Runtime settlement may continue its original workstream within the original user scope, but cannot authorize unrelated work or restart a hold. Initial input uses an empty child seed.

Requests retain the complete human goal, constraints, completion conditions, ordered source inputs and immutable revisions. Delegations refer to that exact version; subsequent necessary stages use its original permission ceiling. Delivery freezes the effective required assignments and references actual reports or terminal outcomes. Reading records and posting progress do not deliver a Request. A successful delivery requires the native tool result, real final reply, completed turn and durable Session flush; complete delivery additionally requires all effective obligations to succeed. Partial delivery records unmet conditions. Recovery reconciles persisted facts without model execution. Background members resume the Lead through native settlement; the Lead ends its arranging turn rather than polling while members run.

While one requirement develops, discuss later requirements in the same Lead conversation. `project_request` records discussion without execution when its disposition is `discussing`; accepted work enters the durable ordered queue. `project_queue` and the Requests panel's matching actions enqueue, move, cancel and explicitly resume requirements. Waiting revisions keep their position. Only the active requirement can delegate work, and its committed complete delivery plus actual drain permits the next requirement's native queue notice. Partial results keep the active requirement open. Cancellation preserves history and drains current owned work before handoff. Cold recovery retains the queue without starting it. Resume targets only the actual current requirement, or the queue head when none is active; rejoining cancelled or released historical work does not clear another requirement's pause.

The registered Lead/worker personas enforce the prompt contract at the model-instruction layer. Host briefs distinguish first assignment from continuation, retain the current delegation identity and scope, and supply the previous recorded report and prerequisite results. Follow-ups preserve correct earlier work; queued acceptance is distinct from actual execution. Prompt wording does not replace host permissions, cancellation or settlement checks.

The worker preset is stable across investigation, document work and development. Project roles explicitly use native tool presentation. The coordinator and read-only/document guards reject arbitrary `run_code` execution as well as shell and unrestricted filesystem tools. The effective scope and exact document paths are durable Project facts. Narrow `project_read`/`project_search` inspect the assigned directory; `project_write_document` writes only declared `.md`, `.mdx`, `.txt`, `.rst` and `.adoc` paths. Necessary stages may use the original Request's permission ceiling; expanding that ceiling or its authorized document paths requires a new actual user message. A stage's permissions become effective only after the worker consumes its new brief. A busy scope change first interrupts and drains the prior activation, then continues the same Session. Native sandbox and delegated permissions remain authoritative.

Normal development uses the selected existing directory. Project workers serialize writes to overlapping canonical directories, including parent/child directories across Projects, until the previous worker and its owned Jobs stop. Independent work within the active requirement, or across Projects, can use read-only members and disjoint sibling directories in parallel. An independent Git worktree is an explicit parallel-development arrangement, never the default; it remains fixed for that workstream and is not registered as an empty sidebar Workspace. The desktop bridge checks its actual branch/identity. Windows checkout enables Git long paths for that command only; it changes no repository or global setting. The user’s selected directory is never reset or deleted.

A newly accepted human development assignment can enable native single-command approval when the Lead permits asking. The exact worker command, working directory and work title appear in the Lead's normal approval composer. Allow once is limited to that pending command; reject and Stop withdraw it. Explicit `never` policy, read-only/document scope, standing sandbox permissions and ordinary Team defaults remain authoritative. Execution captures the consumed assignment's lifetime and checks it immediately before process creation, so a late grant cannot restart stopped work.

## Results and lifecycle

`project_report` records `completed`, `blocked` or `failed`, with a summary, real artifact references, evidence and explicit remaining issues. It then concludes the worker turn. A report alone does not complete the workstream: its delegation must match the current consumed request and the actual native terminal event. A workstream's `done` means the worker reported completion and settled normally; it is not an independent verification claim or delivery of the whole user goal. Project activity shows `done` only for an applicable completed Delivery with no unfinished current requirement. Idle without a report, an interrupted turn, missing input and failures remain recorded; a justified replacement can discharge the original failed obligation without deleting its history.

The native settled notice is the sole proactive worker-to-coordinator notification. `subagent/end` persists its run identity and updates notes. The coordinator’s existing pre-step hook waits for the matching bookkeeping barrier, then adds that run’s recorded reports, artifacts, evidence and remaining issues to the same native message. This covers workers that finish through `project_report` without a closing prose message. Message identity, native source and the single wake remain intact. An old run’s report never replaces a newer delegation’s status or grants new authority. Paused/stopped admission rejects automatic wakeups. Domain facts survive even when an Agent inbox is discarded on disposal; recovery reads them and does not publish synthetic replacement notices. A supplied report alone remains pending. Explicit `project_deliver` records exact report and terminal references, and only its subsequent successful, durably persisted visible reply establishes delivery. Store reads are paged, and unseen results remain pending. This is not a user-read receipt.

Stop first establishes its in-memory hold and real user-message cutoff and cancels owned work; failed persistence or notes cannot prevent cancellation or permit the same request to restart. The durable hold preserves the cutoff across recovery. The existing main composer Cancel hook and natural-language `project_stop` use the same Project stop path. An old coordinator turn cannot delegate itself out of that hold; a new actual user message is required. Workers and their owned Jobs drain; uncertain teardown stays `stopping` with a diagnostic and keeps directory occupancy. External user processes are never killed. Restart marks interrupted activity honestly and starts no model. Resume/restore never starts work automatically. Archive retains all user directories, Session logs and Project materials.

The execution safety hold and the displayed goal state are separate. An unfinished requirement under a hold shows that continuation is needed. A goal with an applicable completed Delivery still shows `done` after cold recovery or Stop, while its persisted hold and user-message cutoff remain intact. Current recovery diagnostics, failed handovers and changed delivery evidence remain visible instead of being hidden by the hold. A newer failed handover draft is current even when an older delivery of the same requirement version completed.

The existing CLI shutdown owner drains Project before closing the Host storage tree. Bare Fiber unload performs runtime cancellation only, since Cordis releases facilities concurrently. After interruption, ordinary `turn/end` and a worker report do not prove the entire activation settled; recovery preserves these as blocked pending facts. Only a persisted native settlement establishes completion. Windows force termination is not a graceful-shutdown guarantee.

The `whale_project_local` storage domain stores projects, requests, deliveries, workstreams, workers and finite delegation/settlement receipts. Catalog content version 2 explicitly migrates the two shipped version-1 formats: the revision/source contract and 0.3.5's currentVersion/authorization/references contract. The existing single-file storage envelope remains version 1. Migration runs atomically before runtime admission and preserves original Project, Lead, member, assignment, report and delivery identities and original 0.3.5 snapshots. Original coordinator Session persistence must establish human authority and the successful declaration/result/final-reply/completed-turn chain. Missing authority remains a visible requirement error requiring a new actual user revision; unproven deliveries remain accessible historical records, without acquiring delivered status or triggering work. Earlier projects acquire no invented request or delivery history. The abandoned Team experiment’s `whale_project` domain remains untouched and is never silently migrated. Session logs are the actual conversation history; notes are a readable projection. Project startup errors produce an unavailable Project service while ordinary Harness conversations remain available. Recovery diagnostics describe current failures and clear after the same roots and original coordinator are successfully inspected; unresolved Team restoration failures are recorded again.

## Materials and UI

```text
$DSH_HOME/projects/<projectId>/
  notes.md
  preferences.md
  charter.md
  decisions.md
  docs/<workstreamId>/
  internal/<workstreamId>/
```

The generated notes section precedes `<!-- whale-project:user-notes -->`; user prose below it is preserved. Preferences are assembled only in the coordinator scope and included in worker briefs, with current user instructions taking precedence. Deliverables are written as new files so earlier results remain available. Private work notes live outside the repository.

`project_read_store` permits only notes, preferences, charter (Project rules), decisions and docs. `charter.md` is user-edited and injected into every Lead step and worker brief; `decisions.md` is appended by the host after durable deliveries and reverts, and its recent entries are injected into the Lead. `requests/changes` and `requests/revert` read and revert one requirement's own changes between its recorded Git baseline and delivery; a revert applies only when it applies cleanly. Worker material writes stay within its own docs/internal roots. Desktop material opening authorizes only this Project’s docs; reported repository artifacts must match their workstream’s fixed authorized directory. Realpath checks reject directory-link escapes.

The client registers its entry only when the Host reports availability. Projects have a separate category below ordinary workspaces, with one entry for their lasting Lead conversation. The conversation header's Requests panel presents per-requirement task cards, each with a minimal strip, a rectangular progress card and full detail; the Team panel beside it shows the Project roster. Both use the native Team action's anchored-panel style beside the normal Lead conversation and open only when asked. Tasks are persisted Requests, not manually created Team assignments. Completed requirements appear as minimal collapsed strips in a list at the bottom of the Requests panel, newest first; each remains independently expandable without hiding active progress. Active and queued requirements remain above them; archived and cancelled records have secondary lists. A card links its real members, work and Delivery; its detail provides Overview, Team, Results and Activity from saved requirement versions, assignments, reports, native settlements and delivery. Task-card archive/restore lives in the card menu. Only an applicable completed Delivery with drained active work can be archived; archive does not stop Team work or archive the Project. If evidence becomes inapplicable, the archived card returns to current as needing review and retains its Restore action.

Project progress lives in the Requests panel. It starts with the current requirement card and collapsed completed strips beneath it; an empty Project shows a short instruction. Card shapes persist per coordinator Session; a closed panel keeps its contents mounted. Records, results, changes and materials open in the Project dialog above the panel. Work rows prioritize actual state and result/stop/retry actions; member history and file changes are in details, with directory, branch and consumed scope disclosed separately. Stopping precedes stopped until actual drain. Project rename/archive/restore remain in the Project row context menu; an active Project archive drains owned work. Project archive replaces the composer with a status notice; archived Projects offer Restore there and protect notes/preferences editing. The Team panel exposes the current native roster and tasks, search, pages and each worker's original records. Worker history retains the original parent/child Session event source and has no second prompt. Task forms, manual dispatch, acceptance and member administration are absent.

Project materials open in the Project dialog with Results, Notes and Project instructions tabs. Results prioritize the Lead's Delivery: its conclusion, key verification, remaining issues and files appear before collapsed delivery details and source reports. Member reports use the same hierarchy, with full report details collapsed. Earlier deliveries and report versions remain available with their original requirement version and recorded time; opening a task-card or progress result selects its exact work and report independently of pagination. Earlier-report counts omit the displayed report. The saved-documents list starts collapsed. File menus expose original locations without replacing recorded authority.

Opening a result file uses the existing native in-app preview or editor while retaining the Materials view. Back to results returns to the same Project, selected version and scroll position, preserving unsaved notes and instructions. File previews show current disk contents; a changed file is identified against its recorded report hash, without rewriting that report. Unsaved tab changes offer save/discard/keep editing, and save failure stays in the current confirmation with the draft intact.

Task-card lists read at most ten Requests per current, completed or archived page; opening one reads its full saved goal, revisions, linked work and Delivery. A completed card requires an applicable completed Delivery of its current revision. Archived cards whose delivery becomes inapplicable surface again in current; Restore clears their saved archive marker. Detail reads return at most 20 current work summaries and three recent historical summaries. Full execution/report data is read only when opening one work. Current work and history use replacement pages, retain the chosen page during polling and reject stale responses. Expanded history follows live revisions without losing its open state; a resumed history anchor explicitly returns to the first historical page. Materials and each work's reports use ten-result replacement pages. Aggregate status describes the entire Project, including preparation and pending summaries, rather than only the visible page.

Queued work identifies the actual prerequisite, directory occupancy or native capacity holding it. Dependency admission checks the current completed receipt and native task together before freezing the supplied prerequisite references; preparation does not read a newer unfinished request as a completed result. Reports retain the references actually consumed by the member. A changed upstream request or replacement report marks the result as having changed prerequisites without rewriting history or restarting completed work.

Only results and native terminal facts actually returned to the Lead can be used in explicit delivery. A real summary or persistence error preserves the result and records the matching Session turn and report or terminal identity. The retry action sends a normal user message to that Lead; it does not replace the draft or dispatch worker work. Historical reports and outcomes without reports remain reachable in ten-item pages. Generated notes prioritize current blocked and active work and reserve a UTF-8 byte budget for the complete legal user notes suffix.

Public authenticated RPCs under `/dsh-project` are `list`, `create`, `detail`, `requests/list`, `requests/get`, `requests/queue`, `requests/archive`, `requests/restore`, `requests/changes`, `requests/revert`, `workstreams/list`, `workstreams/get`, `rename`, `stop`, `pause`, `resume`, `archive`, `restore`, `store/list`, `store/results`, `store/read`, `store/write`, `open` and `diff`. The unprefixed `archive`/`restore` operate on the Project; `requests/archive`/`requests/restore` operate only on one task card. Delegation/reporting are scoped model tools and are not public workbench commands. The desktop patch mounts this plugin and native Team UI. Project reuses an existing Team service or composes one locally; it does not force-enable independent Team settings or edit user patch files.

## Validation boundary

Product implementation, focused Host checks, real provider conversation acceptance, visible desktop acceptance and packaged acceptance are separate evidence. Source or scripted-model checks alone do not certify a real-provider or installer path. This package changes no application version, publishing workflow or main branch.

The later right-side observer and task-card RPCs are source changes. The frozen installed 0.3.5 candidate and its recorded eight-hour observation predate them, so those observations do not establish installed acceptance of this UI or its archive flow.

The configured GPT-6.1-Sol · Codex route has exercised real continuing members, bidirectional peer collaboration with dependent document output, scoped development and local command execution, stop/restore and archive in isolated profiles. The default Node test runner has also passed on the original member through native allow-once approval, preserving the earlier sandbox failure in report history. Current source, packaged observations and installer identity are recorded in [the feature note](../../docs/features/projects.md). These observations do not authorize merging or publishing.

Selected Project directories provide desktop authority through their own durable canonical registrations, without empty ordinary Workspace rows. Creation validates the selected local directory; file/Git/process actions still require the persisted registration. Continuations synchronize the native task description, preserve the original member and only complete after its matching report, settlement and owned Jobs have drained. Peer messages remain bound to both active assignments.
